notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient seen and examined at bedside. 57-year-old male admitted for upper GI bleed. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.46, creatinine 0.76-0.78, hemoglobin 12.6-14.1, platelets 220-224, sodium 138, wbc 8.6-8.7; vitals dbp 78-80, heart_rate 75-80, map 94-96, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-16, sbp 124-131, spo2 96-97, temp 36.5-36.7
Day 0 orders/meds/results: EGD: bleeding duodenal ulcer, treated with endoscopic clips; Pantoprazole 80 mg IV
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Anemia.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.74-0.79, hemoglobin 11.4-12.5, platelets 216-224, sodium 138, wbc 8.4-9; vitals dbp 75-78, heart_rate 75-79, map 91-95, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 123-130, spo2 96-97, temp 36.5-36.7
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Transfuse 1 unit packed red blood cells
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Anemia. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 57-year-old male, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Anemia. Follow up with primary care in one week. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed.
